entries.reason: Not an absence. The default fires when a link carries no LABEL, and a link with no label is one on the candidate's own domain — where "official site" and "campaign site" describe exactly the thing that IS present. The label exists for the two cases where those words would be false: RULING 122's page a party publishes about a candidate, and RULING 145's campaign presence on a platform, both of which name their host instead. So the ?? is choosing between two true descriptions of a link that is there, never standing in front of one that is missing — and when there is no link, neither branch renders at all.

Not a claim about any government. The zip is unknown, so the sentence names the MAP VIEW instead of naming a place we have not established — which is the opposite of the defect: it refuses to put a place name where we have none.

Names only a missing member-name field in our held roll-call projection. It never claims the clerk omitted the name, never substitutes another person, and preserves the recorded vote value independently. This is an OURS field gap under R254.

Names only a missing value in our held roll-call projection. It never infers an abstention, nonattendance, a failed motion or a publisher absence from null, preserving the separate member identity under R254.
An input PLACEHOLDER, not rendered prose about a subject. It tells the reader what to type; it asserts nothing about anything we hold.

Labels an existing roster-source link only when the holder already carries a verbatim sourced term note and sourceUrl. It does not supply a missing note, organization, read date or civic finding. When sourceOrg is absent the link keeps its exact held URL with this record-class label; when the note or URL is absent the fallback never renders. Actual leaf controls in reader-roster-term-note.test.ts prove those boundaries.

Not an absence. This is the LABEL on the disclosure that holds the machine's own words, and the `??` chooses between a caller's own label and the console's standard one. It asserts nothing about any record; a card with nothing to disclose renders no disclosure at all, because the component takes `detail` and returns null when it is absent. The words are the ones §9A.2 names for this slot on every surface.

Not an absence. `needsYou.needed` is already TRUE at this point — the caller has asserted the card needs the owner — and the `??` only chooses wording when the caller named no specific action. So it stands in front of a known YES, never in front of an unknown, and 'Needs you: Yes — a decision from you' is the least specific TRUE sentence rather than a guess about a record. Appears twice: once in NeedsYouLine, once in DefinedTile, which render the same fact in two shapes.

entries.text: no stop reason recorded for this cycle
entries.reason: Not an absence about the world; an absence about the RECORD, stated as one. `fleetSafety.stoppedBecause` is empty when the cycle stopped for no reason it names, and the sentence says exactly that — the runner recorded no reason — rather than 'nothing stopped it', which would be a claim about the cycle. It sits inside Technical details beside the instrument's own words, and the face of the card carries the derived stop sentence or nothing at all.

Not an absence. It is the button's own words, and the `??` chooses between a surface's own label ('Deploy fleet here' on a readiness row) and the console home's. Both describe the same control; neither stands in front of missing data.

entries.text: The fleet has been told where to go.
entries.reason: Not an absence. The `??` fires only after the gateway answered ok, so the action DID happen; the fallback is the sentence to read when the receipt came back without one of its own. It reports a completed write, never a missing record.

entries.text: Working out what this would do…
entries.reason: Not an absence. It is the in-flight state of the preview request — the panel is open and the answer has not arrived — and it is replaced by the preview or by the named reason the preview could not be built. A pending read says it is pending; it never stands in for one that failed.

Not an inferred source disposition. This renders only for an ExactRefusedRecord whose verdict is null, which the projection emits solely from a candidate terminal state carrying a durable failure code or detail. The same row says that the candidate terminal state, rather than a validation receipt, proves it.

entries.text: The intake-runtime reading is unavailable, and this page did not carry a reason.
entries.reason: Names an internal owner-surface gap without claiming that the production store is empty, healthy, or unreachable. It can render only when the observation and its independently derived gap detail are both absent, and deliberately refuses the former default's unsupported claim that no receipt exists.

Names nullable fields inside a structured intake-runtime observation as unread rather than converting them to zero. The observation's outcome and exact flags remain visible, while missing write-alarm or limiter counts license no numeric or health claim. The same reviewed label appears for both count families.

entries.text: The append-only intake observation could not be read safely.
entries.reason: This branch is reached only after the durable row has the expected intake-runtime outcome kind and its contract-level issue check passes, but strict parsing of the embedded observation still returns null. It reports that precise local parse gap and makes no claim about intake health or source activity.

Labels a null field on an existing durable post-deploy integrity receipt, never an absent receipt or an inferred deployment result. It is used for the deployed commit and gate exit independently so neither missing field is filled with success, failure, or a guessed value.

Labels the absent deployedSha field on an existing append-only production-integrity history row. The receipt's recorded outcome, time, detail, and identity still render, but null is not converted into a guessed commit and cannot certify an exact head.

Labels only the aggregateRevision field returned as null by the method-candidate authority projection. The adjacent fail-closed authority state, exact status code, and detail distinguish absence, refusal, and store failure; this text supplies no revision and makes no authority claim.

entries.text: The comparison is unknown, not zero.
entries.reason: The provider reading is present but the independently measured actor comparison is absent. This default explicitly withholds a robot-request count and refuses to turn the missing comparison into zero, so it is a named OURS measurement gap rather than a claim about provider usage.

entries.text: The append-only map-provider history is unavailable, and this panel did not carry a reason.
entries.reason: Names an internal owner-surface gap only when both the projected history and the read outcome detail are absent. It deliberately avoids the former unsupported claim that the canonical history contains no attempts, and makes no assertion about provider activity, LKG, or store reachability.
